sections.heading: Discord without a host
sections.lead: The guild's Discord bot runs on its own server now, always on.
lines: Link your launcher once: /launcher in Discord, then paste the code in Settings > Discord.
After every save (login, /reload, logout) your game's raids and lists reach Discord.
Changes made in Discord reach the game when anyone linked logs in or reloads.
The first game to load them passes them on to everyone online.
Every change from Discord is signed by the bot: the game checks it and ignores fakes.
Guests from Discord wait for a raid leader; lists of non-addon players, for the council.

sections.heading: The launcher
sections.lead: Launcher 0.3.0 updates itself; it has a new Settings > Discord.
lines: Settings > Discord: link, sync now, unlink, and when it last synced.
It asks the bot only while WoW runs, so it stays quiet the rest of the time.
Host mode is gone: nobody's PC has to run the bot any more.

sections.heading: The Binding of Illidan
sections.lead: A roguelike through the Black Temple, played as your own class.
lines: Five floors of random rooms, each ending in a raid boss with its real mechanics.
Magtheridon, Supremus, Teron Gorefiend, Mother Shahraz and Illidan himself.
Your class's bolt is your shot; 18 items, fel bargains and Naaru gifts on the way.
Locked vaults, a goblin vendor and a secret room behind a wall on every floor.
Today's dungeon: one a day for the whole guild; your first try goes on the board.
Fall in a counted run and guildmates find your grave in that room.
Rooms lit by flickering sconces; the Games poster plays the game itself.

sections.heading: Azeromon, alive
sections.lead: Every zone redrawn, with weather, light and a new title screen.
lines: Elwynn, Westfall, Duskwood, Stranglethorn and the mines all redrawn.
Mist in Duskwood, sun shafts and fireflies in the jungle, rain for the whole guild.
Cosy houses and inns: hearths at night, sunlight through the windows by day.
The Guild Hall is a cathedral now: each raid's wing opens with the guild's first kill.
The game fills the whole window; battles have a painted scene for every zone.
A new title screen, and the Games poster plays a film of the zones.
Start menu: MOTION turns the world's motion off.

changelog.title: The Binding of Illidan and a living Azeromon

sections.heading: Loot reserves
sections.lead: Soft reserves for pug nights, in the addon and with the tools pugs already use.
lines: The crest has a new switch, Reserves; its drawer sets 1 to 3 each and opens them.
Who reserved an item rolls on it; one reserve takes it without a roll.
Nobody reserved it: up for grabs, everyone rolls.
Items the guild holds go to the loot council, among guild members, as today.
Pugs reserve by whisper (!sr), in LootReserve's own window, or from softres.it.
Raiders pick from the raid's loot: their BiS items marked, who else is on each.
The drop panel says how each item is decided. Reserves close at the first pull.
Import and export softres.it, Gargul and LootReserve lists; a wrap-up at the end.
Try it: Settings > Demo a roll > Loot reserves, or /dz reserves demo.

sections.heading: Nameplates in our looks
sections.lead: The plates over mobs and players in every look, with casts, threat and your debuffs.
lines: Interface > Looks > Nameplates: they follow your look; Blizzard keeps the game's.
Every caster's cast bar: gold you can kick, grey with a lock you can't.
Tanks see threat in the bar's colour; everyone else gets a glow when close to pulling.
Your own debuffs with their time; the raid's Sunder and curses as an option.
Your target stands out, the others sit back; plates stack instead of overlapping.
Friendly players show their name until they're hurt. Try it shows the Maulgar council.
Health bars slide, and what was just taken off lingers a moment before it drains.

sections.heading: Moving health bars
sections.lead: Unit, party and raid frames in our looks: health slides like the nameplates'.
lines: A hit leaves a pale piece for a moment; it drains into the bar.
Switching targets jumps straight to the new one.
Animated health on each part's page turns it off.

sections.heading: The raid session crest
sections.lead: The session bar is now a small crest showing what waits on the leader and the council.
lines: A round seal: the raid art, a bead per boss and the time; gold counts what waits on you.
Hover it: drops waiting on your vote, loot still to trade, who left, an unlinked raid.
Click it for the drawer: bosses, loot, council, attendance, the planned raid, End raid.
Next boss: Strategy, plus Pull 10 / Break 5 for the leader (DBM and BigWigs see them).
Before the start: the planned raid, who is here, three switches; Start raid in one click.
The switches apply at once; turning the loot council off mid-raid asks first.
In a boss fight it shows only the boss and the fight time, dimmed.
Raiders don't get it, only a pop-up when the raid starts. Settings > Loot > Raid session.
Right-click: hide it for this raid, its settings, or move it in Edit layout.

sections.heading: Main tanks on the raid frames
sections.lead: Each main tank and the mob they hold, by your raid frames, in your look.
lines: One row per main tank: click the tank to target them, the mob beside them to target it.
The mob's half shows its health; red with a name when it turns on someone not a tank.
Before the pull the boss plan's jobs show greyed; the leader sets them all in one click.
Leaders drag rows to reorder (the raid follows); the x at a row's end removes a tank.
Tanks' raid frames wear the shield and their number; threat and boss mods know them.
Raid frames mark your target with a white ring or outline, fainter under the mouse.
In a raid the party frames hide: your group already sits in the raid frames.
Looks > Party and raid: a switch shows them anyway, another turns the tank rows off.

sections.heading: Boss mods
sections.lead: Timers and warnings for every TBC raid boss, off until you switch them on.
lines: Settings > Combat > Boss mods: bars, warnings and sounds for what wipes raids.
Every alert has its own switch; tank and healer alerts go only to that role.
Timers where the sources disagree count to the earliest time, then say 'within n s'.
/dz pull 10 and /dz break 5 reach DBM and BigWigs users too, and theirs reach you.
Hyjal: the next wave and 'Wave 4 of 8'. A range frame where the game can measure.
Your UI look or one of their own, a size of your choice, and a Try it for every fight.

sections.heading: Boss mods that learn
sections.lead: Timers tighten from our own pulls, and never change in the middle of one.
lines: A timer moves only when 3 clean pulls agree on when the boss really casts.
Never more than a quarter away from DBM's and BigWigs' numbers.
A pull always runs on the timers it started with; bars follow the real casts.
A small line over the bars says a pull is recorded; a striped end shows the window.
After a pull that changed something, one note says what we learned.
Your pulls and the guild's fill each other's gaps: shared after the pull, checked first.
Settings > Boss mods > Bosses: each boss's page shows what every timer learned.
Turn off 'Learn from our pulls' to keep DBM's and BigWigs' numbers.

sections.heading: Raids on Discord
sections.lead: Our raids posted on the guild's Discord, with sign-ups right there.
lines: The GM picks the Discord channels under Settings > Guild > Discord.
Each raid gets a post in the addon's look; it updates as people sign up.
Sign up from Discord: make your character there once (name, class, spec).
/raids lists the coming raids, /bis shows your list as a gear sheet to edit.
A reminder by DM an hour before; Running late or Can't make it tell the leader.
A small Discord mark after the names of characters made in Discord.

sections.heading: Settings, sorted
sections.lead: Six groups, a search, and every look in one place.
lines: A rail of six groups, each with a line saying how it is set: General to Guild.
A group opens as tiles, one per feature: how it is set, and its on/off switch.
A tile opens the feature's page: main options first, the rest under More options.
A feature that is off shows one box with Switch on (and Try it), not greyed rows.
Options that need another switch on, like the threat warning, show only then.
Search finds any option, with a working switch; click its name to go there.
A gold dot marks what you changed; Back to defaults puts a card as it came.
Alerts: the BiS toast, its sound and chat line are now a row of the pop-up grid.
Interface > Looks: every look in one place, a page and a live sample per part.
Meter, class bar and timer themes moved there; their cards link to them.
Help, demo mode and About sit at the rail's foot; the GM's checklist is under Guild.

sections.heading: Wardrobe: outfits in one click
sections.lead: Outfits in one click: swaps everything at once; weapons even in combat.
lines: Gear > Wardrobe: save what you wear, or your BiS list, as an outfit.
Each slot shows what Wear does: swaps in, in the bank, missing or keep current.
Wear swaps only what differs, all at once. In a fight the armour waits for the end.
With the bank open, the pieces in it come out to your bags first.
Wear automatically: a spec switch, a boss or zone, a fishing pole, a mount.
The quick-swap bar: a button per outfit in your bar theme; Edit layout moves it.
A key for Next outfit under Key Bindings > AddOns; /dz wardrobe opens it.

sections.heading: The game's UI in DisasterZone's looks
sections.lead: Flat, Halo, Sigil, Slate or Gilded for the frames you play with.
lines: Settings > Interface > Looks: one look for everything, or one of its own per part.
Unit frames: player, target, target of target, focus and pet, with combo points.
Health numbers sit inside the health bar; a long name is cut short, never drawn over them.
Party and raid frames in the same looks: range fade, and a light on what you can dispel.
Halo raid frames: capsules with name and missing health, a ring lit by dispels or aggro.
Cast bars: your latency at the end of your casts, a lock on casts you can't interrupt.
Action bars keep the game's buttons, in the look's frame, keys and range colour.
Minimap: round or square, the look's edge, zone and clock; addon buttons tidied away.
Blizzard stays the default: nothing changes until you pick a look.
Switching a replaced part back to the game's frames takes a reload (it asks).

sections.heading: Classic: our layouts in the game's own art
sections.lead: A seventh look: the Dock, bags and frames dressed in the game's textures.
lines: Looks > Use Classic everywhere: frames, meters, class bars and timers at once.
Bar art for the Dock: Ironforge stone, Stormwind marble and gold, or the Guild Vault.
Stance and aura buttons stand on a step; at max level a band fills the experience slot.
Gryphons or lions at its ends match the art, or pick your own (or none).
Buttons wear the game's action button frame, its hover, pressed and proc glows.
Bags: the backpack grown into one window, a carved slot for every item.
Unit frames: the game's target frame, the gold dragon on bosses and elites.
Raid frames are the game's own cells; cast bars wear its border and shield.
Meters in the tooltip's frame; Blessings and totems as action buttons.
The swing and shot timers drawn as a cast bar, the next press in the spell alert.
Health is the game's green in Classic; raid cells stay in class colours.

sections.heading: Combat text in every look
sections.lead: Your hits, heals and procs as numbers on screen, each look with a move of its own.
lines: Looks > Combat text: off until you turn it on; numbers ride the mob's nameplate.
Flat: hits that land together, Windfury and ticks, count up as one line.
Halo: a crit fires a ring; Consecration's ticks circle the target like a clock.
Sigil: numbers stamp down, a crit's tile shatters, tally pips count the ticks.
Slate: a quiet feed beside the target, a hairline under each hit for its size.
Gilded: gold and silver numbers, sparks off crits, big crits in a gold frame.
Classic: the game's damage font, Hammer of Wrath! in its button's glow, low health.
Hits taken and heals beside you, with the healer's name; procs and alerts on top.
The game's own combat text steps aside while ours is on, and comes back after.
Try it plays a made-up pull. Edit layout moves you, the target spot and the alerts.

sections.heading: Edit layout: everything on your screen, in one place
sections.lead: Move, line up and mirror every frame at once: /dz edit.
lines: Every DisasterZone frame gets a faint dashed outline; the one you pick turns gold.
One slim bar at the top: what you picked, its tools, Grid, Snap, Names, Frames.
The bar fades back when the frame you picked is under it, and while you drag.
The game's own frames too: player, target, cast bar, action bars, minimap, buffs.
Frames snap to the middle of the screen (gold) and line up with each other (teal).
Drop a frame between two others and it lands exactly halfway (pink gaps).
Mirror two frames: move one and the other follows on the far side of the centre.
Pick several: line up their edges, give them equal gaps or centre them as a group.
Arrow keys move 1 px, Shift a grid step; hold Alt to place freely; Ctrl+Z undoes.
Frames that only show sometimes (rolls, the raid bar, reminders) show while you edit.

sections.heading: Resize anything in Edit layout
lines: Pull a corner handle to scale a frame; Shift scales from its middle.
Side handles stretch cast bars and the XP bar wider or narrower.
Roll the mouse wheel over a picked frame: 5% a notch. Double-click a handle: 100%.
Pick several and they grow together, gaps and all.
The game's frames too, in the steps their own Edit Mode allows.
The game's Esc menu has a DisasterZone layout button, right under Edit Mode.
Fixed: the roll frame and raid session bar went back to their default spot after a reload.
Fixed: Addon buttons > In a drawer now gathers the minimap buttons under the ··· knob.

sections.heading: Layout profiles
lines: Each character picks its own profile: Raid, Solo, Healing, whatever you make.
Share a profile in chat: a guildmate who clicks the link can keep it.
Settings > Layout, or the minimap: pin Edit layout to the arc.

sections.heading: No more Locked switches
lines: Meters, the swing and shot timers and the class bars move in Edit layout now.
Their Locked switches are gone; /dz swing unlock (and the others) open Edit layout.
Where you had put them is kept.

sections.heading: Swing and shot timers: rotation optional
lines: Settings > Show rotation off hides the next presses and plan lane: just the timer.

sections.heading: The Dock: every bottom bar on one grid
sections.lead: Action bars, bags, menu, stance, pet and XP built as one piece.
lines: Bars 1 to 3 make one block; bags and the menu stand beside it at its exact height.
Stance and pet bars line up on top; the XP bar runs the block's width under it.
One plate behind it all in the look, with seams between the parts (Halo floats).
Bars 4 and 5 stand at the right edge in the same size and look.
Bar 1's page arrows get a slim strip beside the block, the page number between them.
Looks > Action bars: button size from Compact to Large; move it in Edit layout.
Every look made over: Halo's rings, Sigil and Gilded's gold, Slate's table show the state.

sections.heading: Bags, key ring and bank in your look
sections.lead: One window for your bags, one for the bank, in the Dock's size and look.
lines: Three layouts: One bag (the default), Shelves sorted by kind, or Bag by bag.
Shelves fold; Junk sells in one click at a vendor; new items glow until you look.
Search as you type, by name or type; junk and new work as words too.
Sort stacks partial stacks and orders everything at once: a full bag in under a second.
The key ring folds into the bags from the Dock's key ring or the footer.
At a banker the Bank window opens beside your bags, with bank bag slots to buy.
Items keep their slots: clicking, dragging and using them work exactly as before.

sections.heading: Themes for the swing and shot timers
lines: Halo, Sigil, Slate, Gilded or Pips: the same looks as the Blessings and Totem bars.
Each timer picks its own in Settings > Interface > Looks > Timers.
Point at a theme to see it on your timer; the plan lane comes in the same look.

changelog.title: Edit layout and the UI in our looks

sections.heading: Council Bingo: a new card set
sections.lead: Every square is a named raid moment now.
lines: Every square is a named moment with its spell's icon: Bubble Hearth, Leeroy, Mrglglgl.
Five qualities like items: common, uncommon, rare, epic and legendary.
Every card is dealt the same mix: 1 legendary, 2 epic, 4 rare, 7 uncommon, 10 common.
Each raid has its own pool of 10+ squares; up to 6 of yours come from it in there.
Piranha Snack, Wolf Pack, Nova Party, Rock Bottom, What Goes Up: every raid has its own.
The /roll filler is gone: one roll square is left (Critical Fail).

sections.heading: Council Bingo: rarity that means something
sections.lead: The rarer the square, the louder it lands.
lines: Points by quality (1, 2, 3, 5, 10) plus 10 a line; the season ladder counts points.
Rare squares on your card pop a toast; epic ones toast the whole raid.
A legendary takes over the card for everyone, with the legendary loot toast.
Fated: when your legendary goes off it also daubs your best gap. It can win you the night.
A line one square short gets a gold thread, and 1 AWAY on the square you need.
The header says which line is one away; the race shows everyone's card as a dot map.

sections.heading: Council Bingo: the Codex
lines: A Codex tab beside the card: every square, a silhouette until you've seen it happen.
Point at one for who set it off first, where, and how often you've seen it.
The season ladder and the legendaries you've witnessed sit beside it.
Demo mode shows a made-up game, with a button to try how each quality arrives.

sections.heading: Shot timer (Hunters)
sections.lead: The swing timer's ring, for Auto Shot and Steady Shot.
lines: New shot timer for every Hunter spec: the swing timer's ring, timed to your Auto Shot.
The orange window is when Steady Shot still fits before the next Auto Shot.
The red end is the next shot's windup: stand still and cast nothing there.
What to press comes from WoWSims' Hunter rotation, the one the gear sim plays.
Steady Shot when it fits, else Multi-Shot, else Arcane Shot; Kill Command after a crit.
Haste is read live: quiver, Rapid Fire, Bloodlust and haste rating all move the window.
Aspect hints: Viper when you run dry, Hawk once you have mana again.
After a fight: Auto Shots on time, clipped (and the time lost) and held by moving.
It skips shots you'd get under a quarter second to press (Reaction time in Settings).
Settings > Class tools > Shot timer; /dz shot. Demo mode plays the rotation by itself.

sections.heading: Swing and shot timers: see the next press coming
lines: The icon in the middle now has a cooldown swipe, like your action bars.
The dark part shrinks as the press comes closer; full colour means press it now.

sections.heading: Prized items: recipes and formulas
lines: New rule Profession: Enchanting 375 or higher (any profession, any skill).
Their alts can count, and someone who already knows the recipe can be left out.
Recipe / formula start: adding a recipe sets the profession and skill from the item.

sections.heading: Polls: several questions in one

lines.text: A poll can ask up to five questions, each with its own kind and answers.
New poll: + Question adds one; who votes and when it closes are the whole poll's.
You answer question by question: it moves on to the next one by itself.

lines: Players still on an older version see each question as a poll of its own.

sections.heading: Your alts can change what you made
lines: Strategies, polls and events you made: edit or remove them from any of your characters.
(Members still on 1.4.0 see those changes once they update.)

sections.heading: Fixes
lines: Deleted events and polls no longer come back when someone away for weeks logs in.
Removed prized items and deleted strategies stay gone after a long break too.
Calendar events and polls past their keep time no longer return from an old copy.
Reviews of an event deleted long ago no longer come back with it.
Chess: Resign asks first, so a stray click no longer ends your game.
The next raid's countdown and "Pause pop-ups for an hour" follow the server's clock.
Members: "Last seen in" times follow the server's clock too.
Members: unlocking someone's main is a lock icon, shown only while a raid runs.
Dungeon run notes are no longer cut in the middle of an accented letter.
Guests and pugs show in their class colour in more places.
The Events and Dungeons pages draw once when you open them, not twice.
